abstract:
<jats:title>Summary</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Bread wheat is a leading cereal crop worldwide. Limited amount of superior allele loci restricted the progress of molecular improvement in wheat breeding. Here, we revealed new allelic variation distribution for 13 yield‐related traits in series of genome‐wide association studies (
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GWAS</jats:styled-content>
                    ) using the wheat 90K genotyping assay, characterized in 163 bread wheat cultivars. Agronomic traits were investigated in 14 environments at three locations over 3 years. After filtering
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    data sets,
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GWAS</jats:styled-content>
                    using 20 689 high‐quality
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    s associated 1769 significant loci that explained, on average, ~20% of the phenotypic variation, both detected already reported loci and new promising genomic regions. Of these, repetitive and pleiotropic
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    s on chromosomes 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">AS</jats:styled-content>
                    , 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">AL</jats:styled-content>
                    , 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BS</jats:styled-content>
                    , 5
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BL</jats:styled-content>
                    and 7
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">AS</jats:styled-content>
                    were significantly linked to thousand kernel weight, for example
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BS</jats:styled-content>
                    00021705_51 on 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BS</jats:styled-content>
                    and wsnp_Ex_c32624_41252144 on 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">AS</jats:styled-content>
                    , with phenotypic variation explained (
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PVE</jats:styled-content>
                    ) of ~24%, consistently identified in 12 and 13 of the 14 environments, respectively. Kernel length‐related
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    s were mainly identified on chromosomes 7
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BS</jats:styled-content>
                    , 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">AS</jats:styled-content>
                    , 5
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">AL</jats:styled-content>
                    and 5
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BL</jats:styled-content>
                    . Plant height‐related
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    s on chromosomes 4
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">DS</jats:styled-content>
                    , 6
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">DL</jats:styled-content>
                    , 2
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">DS</jats:styled-content>
                    and 1
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">BL</jats:styled-content>
                    were, respectively, identified in more than 11 environments, with averaged
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PVE</jats:styled-content>
                    of ~55%. Four
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    s were confirmed to be important genetic loci in two
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">RIL</jats:styled-content>
                    populations. Based on repetivity and
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PVE</jats:styled-content>
                    , a total of 41
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    loci possibly played the key role in modulating yield‐related traits of the cultivars surveyed. Distribution of superior alleles at the 41
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    loci indicated that superior alleles were getting popular with time and modern cultivars had integrated many superior alleles, especially for peduncle length‐ and plant height‐related superior alleles. However, there were still 19
                    <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>
                    loci showing less than percentages of 50% in modern cultivars, suggesting they should be paid more attention to improve yield‐related traits of cultivars in the Yellow and Huai wheat region. This study could provide useful information for dissection of yield‐related traits and valuable genetic loci for marker‐assisted selection in Chinese wheat breeding programme.
                  </jats:p>
title: Genome‐wide association study for 13 agronomic traits reveals distribution of superior alleles in bread wheat from the Yellow and Huai Valley of China
